newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN STOCKS END DOWN IN CAUTION-MIRED MARKET.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN STOCKS END DOWN IN CAUTION-MIRED MARKET.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly lower on Thursday in narrow, cautious trading, failing to take a cue from Wall Street's record overnight rise as investors baulked at resuming the price-chase, brokers said.
The weighted index lost 20.59 points or 0.21 percent to close at 9,840.88 points.
Turnover was relatively moderate at T$160 billion.

Taiwan's index, which has gained more than 40 percent in 1997 but has stalled in the past few sessions after a dramatic punch though 10,000 points, was impassive even in the face of Wall Street's overnight record highs.
Brokers said sentiment was dampened further by recently soaring money rates that tightened investment liquidity.
"The market still has further room to grow, but it will probably continue this downward consolidation for the near term," said Amy Huang, analyst for Nomura Securities.
"Right now the index is just trying a find firm support."
Electronics shares, which have spearheaded Taiwan's yearlong rally, continued their recent profit-taking streak and closed 1.54 percent lower as a sector.
Microchip company Winbond dropped T$5.50 to T$76, fellow chipmaker United Microelectronics fell T$3 to T$134 and computer giant Acer Inc lost T$3 to T$97.
Financials gained a moderate 0.40 percent, but momentum was curbed by the government's ongoing auction of 418 million shares in state-run Chiao Tung Bank.
The auction was scheduled to end on Friday.
The only sector to reap significant gains was construction shares, a relatively low-priced sector that soared 4.52 percent on bargain-hunting, brokers said.
